attempts.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as router between lan-a (node2, 10.50.10.0/24) and lan-b (node3, 10.50.20.0/24) using pure IP forwarding (no NAT), so node2 and node3 reach each other on any port with original source addresses preserved. Verified with ICMP and arbitrary-port TCP tests in both directions, confirmed no NAT rules exist on node1 and node3 sees node2's real LAN-A IP as the TCP peer address. Adjusted firewalld on node2/node3 to trust the new LAN interfaces so arbitrary ports aren't blocked. Completed mandatory restart protocol: rebooted node1, node2, and node3 sequentially (one at a time), proved boot_id changes on each, and confirmed interface config, routes, firewall zones, and full end-to-end connectivity recovered after each restart.
